title: Alternating permutations, Euler numbers, and the cd-index of S_n
key_idea: An **alternating permutation** satisfies $w(1) < w(2) > w(3) < w(4) > \cdots$. Their count is the **tangent/secant number** $E_n$ (Euler number), which appears in the Taylor series $\tan x = \sum_{n \text{ odd}} E_n x^n/n!$ and $\sec x = \sum_{n \text{ even}} E_n x^n/n!$. The **cd-index** is a polynomial in non-commuting variables $c$ and $d$ that encodes all descent-set statistics of $S_n$ compactly.
summary: **To be filled in when you reach this section.** Three subsections: (1.6.1) basic properties of $E_n$ and the generating function; (1.6.2) bijection via increasing binary trees (flip equivalence); (1.6.3) min-max trees and the $cd$-index $\Psi(S_n)$.

notation.description: cd-index of a graded poset $P$ (or of $S_n$): a polynomial in $c,d$ encoding flag $f$-vector data
